newsitem.title: DENMARK: GN Store Nord sees Sonofon profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GN Store Nord sees Sonofon profit in 1997.

text.p: Danish cable group GN Store Nord forecast on Wednesday that its partly-owned Sonofon mobile telephone unit would make a profit in 1997, the first since it was founded in 1993.
"Despite new investment in Sonofon, the company will move into profit from 1997," GN Store Nord managing director Thomas F.Duer told a news conference.
He did not forecast the 1996 result but has said before that it would be better than 1995's 127 million crown pre-tax loss.
Sonofon and its rival, state-run Tele Danmark, have spent huge amounts in a cut-throat battle for market share.

Duer said Sonofon was already showing a positive cash flow on its operations and that it expected its total 2.5 to three billion crown investment, including the setting up of a new GSM mobile phone network, to be repaid by 2003.
In 1993 Sonofon set itself a target of 200,000 mobile phone subscribers by 2002, but already has around 500,000.
About 1.3 million Danes currently have mobile phones, with about 800,000 -- or 62 percent -- subscribing to Tele Danmark.
GN Store Nord said on Wednesday that it and U.S. ally BellSouth had bought Swedish firm NordicTel's minority share in Sonofon, becoming joint sole owners.
BellSouth now holds 46.5 percent of Sonofon, while GN Store Nord's stake is 53.5 percent.
